name: Weapon Loadout
description: Owns the answer to 'what am I holding and what does pulling the trigger mean right now': active slot, swap order, and fire mode. It does not spawn projectiles — it translates trigger intent into combat.fireRequested with the resolved weapon stats attached, and combat.projectile_system takes it from there. It does not count bullets either: combat.ammo_economy listens to the same event and owns the magazine, so a dry fire is rejected by the economy rather than by a second conditional here. Slot count is deliberately small and fixed per config; inventory breadth — how many weapons you own at all — is inventory.core_inventory's problem, and conflating the two is how shooters accidentally become inventory managers.

inputs.name: slotCount
inputs.description: Weapons carried and hot-swappable. Two is the genre default because a third slot turns mid-fight decisions into menu navigation. Excess weapons stay in inventory, not here.

inputs.name: swapTimeSeconds
inputs.description: Dead time between requesting a swap and the new weapon being able to fire. This is the tax that makes weapon choice a commitment; setting it to 0 makes slot count meaningless.

inputs.name: availableFireModes
inputs.description: Fire modes the equipped weapon profile may declare. The loadout validates a weapon's mode against this list rather than trusting the data, because a typo'd mode otherwise fails silently at the trigger.

inputs.name: burstCount
inputs.description: Shots per trigger pull in burst mode. Burst exists as a first-class mode, not a macro over semi-auto, because burst pacing (the pause BETWEEN bursts) is a balance lever semi cannot express.

inputs.name: autoFireRatePerSecond
inputs.description: Maximum request rate in auto mode. The loadout gates trigger intent at this rate; it never asks combat.ammo_economy whether the shot is affordable — that rejection comes back as its own event.

outputs.name: activeSlot
outputs.description: Index of the currently equipped slot. UI reads this; gameplay logic should read the weapon profile carried on combat.fireRequested instead.

outputs.name: activeFireMode
outputs.description: The mode the next trigger pull will use.

outputs.name: isSwapping
outputs.description: True during the swap dead time. Fire requests arriving now are buffered, not dropped, so a swap-cancel feels responsive rather than eaten.
